capitals.name: Marienwerder (Kwidzyn)
capitals.note: The page says the capital 'alternated between Marienwerder (Kwidzyn) and Danzig (Gdańsk) during its early existence' (no years). Danzig was Polish until 1793 (Gdańsk page: annexed 1793, restored to Prussia in 1815 'and became the capital of Regierungsbezirk Danzig'), so 1773-1792 is Marienwerder alone; the Kwidzyn page calls it 'the capital of the District of Marienwerder' (no date). After 1793 the alternation has no years on any page opened; Marienwerder is kept as the one booked capital (a bridge).

correction.text: West Prussia of 1773: Royal Prussia without Danzig and Thorn, with the formerly East Prussian Marienwerder district

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; its Kingdom of Prussia shapes draw the land). 'In 1773, the territories annexed by Prussia became the new province of West Prussia' (First Partition page). Redrawn after review: the first shape was the gazetteer region 'West Prussia' with a 70 km Netze circle (46,534 km2 without Warmia), which drew the whole Kuyavian-Pomeranian voivodeship (Włocławek and the Brześć Kujawski voivodeship, Polish until 1793), Słupsk and Lębork and left out Elbląg; 22% (10,369 km2) of it lay inside Cliopatria's Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth shape for 1780. Now Royal Prussia (the royal-prussia shape) without Danzig and Thorn plus the formerly East Prussian Marienwerder district ('incorporated into the province of West Prussia the following year, along with the formerly East Prussian Marienwerder Kreis', Province page; the Kwidzyn page dates the transfer 1772): 20,240 km2 on the grid. The Netze District is a separate territory until 1775 (Province page: 'Parts of Greater Poland and Kuyavia formed a separate Netze District located to the south'), and Warmia 'became part of East Prussia'. Check against the page's 36,000 km2 share of 1772 (most of Royal Prussia with Warmia, the Netze District and northern Kuyavia): 20,240 + Netze 12,144 + Warmia 5,060 = 37,444 km2, ratio 1.04.

correction.text: West Prussia with the Netze District, administered with it from 1775

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'from 1775 onwards the Netze District was administered with West Prussia' (Netze District page); it 'was formed from the annexed Poznań and Gniezno Voivodeships and the Kuyavian lands of western Inowrocław Voivodeship along the river', with the divisions Wałcz, Kamień, Bydgoszcz and Inowrocław. Drawn as a polygon along the Noteć (Wałcz and Kamień in the north-west to Bydgoszcz and Inowrocław in the south-east) minus Royal Prussia: 12,144 km2 (the page gives no area); with the Netze District the province is 32,384 km2 on the grid. Replaces the 70 km circle at 17.4 E, 53.1 N. Inowrocław is inside, as the Netze page names it (the Second Partition page lists the Inowrocław voivodeship in South Prussia's 1793 land: the voivodeship was split, the western part going in 1772).

correction.text: West Prussia with Danzig and Thorn, 1793

keyframe_review.note: 1793: 'Further Polish areas were annexed in the Second Partition of Poland in 1793'; this added Danzig and Thorn (Gdańsk page: 'Danzig was annexed by the Kingdom of Prussia in 1793'). 35,673 km2 on the grid. Redrawn after review so that the Chełmno Land and Toruń are West Prussia's and the Brześć Kujawski voivodeship and Dobrzyń Land are south-prussia's (22,761-27,060 km2 of double drawing before; overlap with south-prussia now 0).

correction.text: West Prussia without the Free City of Danzig, the Thorn and Kulm country and the southern Netze District, 1807-1814

keyframe_review.note: 1807: 'it also lost Danzig, which was a Free City from 1807 until 1814'; 'West Prussia lost its southern territory in the vicinity of Thorn and Kulm' to the Duchy of Warsaw. The Netze District page: 'large parts of the southern district went to the Bydgoszcz Department of the Duchy of Warsaw. The northwestern area around Wałcz and Kamień was incorporated into West Prussia.' So the shape keeps the Wałcz-Kamień (Deutsch Krone and Flatow) part of the Netze District and drops Bydgoszcz and Inowrocław: 20,493 km2.

keyframe_review.note: 1815: 'Danzig, Kulm, and Thorn were returned to West Prussia'; 'In 1815, the province was administratively subdivided into the Regierungsbezirke Danzig and Marienwerder'; Greater Poland areas of the 1772 Netze District 'were added to West Prussia as well', 'The remainder became part of the Grand Duchy of Posen' (Netze page: the Wałcz-Kamień part 'belonged to the Marienwerder Region of West Prussia'; the Netze page dates its incorporation 1807, the Province page 1815). West Prussia joined East Prussia in personal union in 1824 and was officially combined in 1829 into the Province of Prussia; the shape stands to 1828. Redrawn after review: the old shape kept the 70 km Netze circle and southern Kuyavia (Bydgoszcz and Inowrocław, Posen's after 1815; Włocławek, Congress Poland) and was 49,568 km2 (ratio 1.94 to the 25,580 km2 of 1910). Now 26,818 km2, ratio 1.05 (disc tests: Bydgoszcz, Inowrocław, Włocławek, Piła, Nakło, Słupsk, Lębork outside; Wałcz, Złotów, Sępólno, Kwidzyn, Elbląg, Toruń, Gdańsk inside).

region.text: West Prussia of 1773: Royal Prussia without Danzig and Thorn, with the formerly East Prussian Marienwerder district

ledger.note: 1773: 'West Prussia was established as a province of the Kingdom of Prussia in 1773'; 'The Partition Sejm ratified the cession on 30 September 1773'. Prussia took most of Royal Prussia, the Netze District and northern Kuyavia, 36,000 km2 and about 600,000 people, not Danzig or Thorn. Shape redrawn after review (see the keyframe note): the province of 1773 holds Royal Prussia without Danzig and Thorn and the Marienwerder district; the Netze District (12,144 km2) joins in 1775 and Warmia goes to East Prussia.

1807: 'it also lost Danzig, which was a Free City from 1807 until 1814'.

notes:
The Prussian partition zone of 1772, a state Cliopatria lacks, and the successor of royal-prussia. Typed colony (province of kingdom-of-prussia, later the German Empire). Lives 1773-1829 and 1878-1919 with the 1829 merger and the 1878 restoration as events; the keyframes leave 1829-1877 empty. The pages opened give nothing for 1829-1877 except the Province of Prussia. The scope of eu-15 is to 1789; the events after 1795 rest on the Province page and the Netze District page.

Repaired after the review (2026-10-31): (1) The gazetteer region 'West Prussia' (Pomeranian + Kuyavian-Pomeranian voivodeships) and the 70 km Netze circle are gone. The shape is built from the royal-prussia shape (see its dossier), the Marienwerder district, a Netze District polygon minus Royal Prussia and, after 1815, only its Wałcz-Kamień part; 20,240 km2 in 1773, 32,384 in 1775, 35,673 in 1793, 20,493 in 1807, 26,818 in 1815-1918 (page 25,580 for 1910, ratio 1.05; was 49,568). (2) The Kuyavia line with south-prussia: Brześć Kujawski and Dobrzyń to South Prussia; Chełmno Land and Toruń to West Prussia; Inowrocław and Bydgoszcz to the Netze District, West Prussia 1775-1807; overlap 0. (3) The Netze District joins in 1775 (it was a separate territory 1772-1774) and its southern part leaves in 1807 (new events). (4) Capital: Danzig was Polish before 1793, so 1773-1792 is Marienwerder alone; the later alternation has no years on any page.

Not settled: (1) The Netze District has no dossier; counterpart is its name. The Netze page says its Wałcz-Kamień part was incorporated into West Prussia in 1807 and the Province page says 'added' in 1815; I draw it from 1807. (2) The 1919 loss regions are a reading: the page gives only 'eastern territory ... Region of West Prussia' and 'western remainder ... Posen'; Poland and Danzig come to 70% of the drawn province against the page's 62%. (3) 'Dissolved' 1919 (lead) against 1920 (body). (4) The Marienwerder transfer: the Province page says 1773 ('the following year'), the Kwidzyn page 1772; the shape includes it from 1773. (5) Counterpart 'Province of Prussia' is a name, not a dossier; 'free-city-of-danzig' (Cliopatria 1809-1939) is used for the 1807-1814 Napoleonic city and the 1919 Free City alike. (6) Warmia, in Royal Prussia's old territory, is not West Prussia (East Prussia from 1773). (7) The gazetteer lacks regions for Royal Prussia, the Chełmno Land, the Netze District and the Brześć Kujawski Voivodeship; 'West Prussia' (alt name Royal Prussia) is the Pomeranian + Kuyavian-Pomeranian voivodeships and misleads.
